_README: C154. Re-adjudication of all 26 UNREACHABLE verdicts in reports/c138_known_gaps_ledger.md section 4, against the C153 rule 'trace the raise site to the caller that actually reaches it'. Regenerate with scripts/c154_unreachable_readjudication.py --write, from a checkout with a built pokemon-showdown; CI builds none, so nothing re-derives the POOL half against a live pool. The CITATION half is re-derived on every run of tests/test_unreachable_readjudication.py. NEVER edit this by hand to make a test pass: the pin compares the ledger against it, so a hand edit silently moves a verdict. It lives under tests/data/ and NOT under reports/ on purpose -- see the module docstring, it is keyed by counter names.

R1.candidate: Future Sight / Doom Desire -- residual order 11 and the `future_sight_pending` refusal
R1.correction: ⚠ Two things the row does not say, and the second is the one that decides the verdict. (1) The payload ALWAYS CARRIES the key -- `src/pokezero/local_showdown.py:2359` is unconditional -- so the closure is 'the mapping is always EMPTY', never 'the key is absent'. That is the exact distinction C153 drew for `deferred_opponent_action` and did not carry over to this row. (2) **The repo ships a Custom Game scenario that casts Future Sight** (`src/pokezero/golden_corpus_scenarios.py:469`, an Alakazam with the move and a scripted preference for it), so the raise is constructible from committed code. What keeps it unreached is that the spec sits in `interaction_registry_specs()` (`:353`) and not `scenario_specs()` (`:109`), and every world-building harness -- including `run_scenario_fallback_sweep` (`:578`) -- defaults to the latter. That is a ONE-KEYWORD-ARGUMENT closure: passing `specs=interaction_registry_specs()` fires the raise immediately. 'Dead code in this format' is right; 'retired' would not be.
R1.demonstration: `_reject_unsupported_globals` raises at `src/pokezero/engine_world.py:926` when `payload['futureSight']` has any nonzero value. THE PAYLOAD IS NOT THE DIFFERENTIAL'S: `world_battle_spec` builds its own at `src/pokezero/engine_world.py:883` and reaches the guard at `:397`, and `_public_materialization_payload` fills the key from `replay.future_sight` at `src/pokezero/local_showdown.py:2359`. That mapping has exactly one writer, `_update_future_sight` at `src/pokezero/showdown.py:4947`, gated at `:4940` on the protocol effect id being in `_FUTURE_MOVES` = `{futuresight, doomdesire}`. Both are 0 of 220 species, so the mapping is EMPTY for every gen3 randbats battle and an empty dict makes `any(...)` false -- the guard cannot fire FOR ANY CALLER of `world_battle_spec`. Residual order 11 has the same single trigger class.
R1.foreclosure_note: constructible from committed code -- `golden_corpus_scenarios.py`'s `future_sight_pending` spec -- and foreclosed only by which spec list the harnesses default to

R10.correction: ⚠ Three upgrades, and the first changes the strength of the verdict. (1) The row argues the bucket is UNAMBIGUOUS; it is in fact UNEMITTABLE, because every production path into `heal_subcase` starts in `render_move_phase`'s Sleep Talk block and no set pairs `sleeptalk` with a drain move (0 of 393). The row reasons from the bucket's NAME and never traces its caller -- the exact shape the C153 rule forbids. ⚠ **And the first revision of THIS correction did it too**, in the same sentence that names the failure: it asserted, untraced, that `heal_subcase` is reached only through `ambiguous_unrenderable_slug_with_protect`. There are two routes; review found the second. The conclusion held, the sentence did not, and nothing re-derived it -- so the graph is now built by `rust_call_graph` and pinned. (2) "the pool's only drain move is `gigadrain`" was an assertion; it is now the `drain`-flagged subset of the pool's 125 moves, derived from the dex, with the five gen3 drain moves it excludes named. (3) The Shell Bell half rests on the same generation-time item argument R6 does and needs the same runtime clause: the pool's only item-moving moves SWAP (`trick`) or REMOVE (`knockoff`) and no gen3 mechanism creates an item. ⚠ One site the row's sentence does not cover survives as a note: the NAMED (non-Sleep-Talk) renderer tags a heal `[from] drain` whenever `choice.drain.is_some()`, and Shell Bell sets that field, so a Shell Bell holder would be mislabelled there too -- same unreachability, second site.
R10.demonstration: `heal_subcase` (`rust/pokezero-search/src/events.rs:3949`) routes a positive ATTACKER-side heal with foe damage in the same tail to `heal_drain_or_shellbell` at `:3962`. ⚠ THE BUCKET HAS ONE PRODUCTION EMITTER AND THE ROW DOES NOT NAME IT. The caller graph is DERIVED, not asserted (see `heal_subcase_call_graph`): the crate entry point `['branch_events']` reaches `heal_subcase` only through `render_move_phase`, whose remaining 5 graph roots are thin non-`_with_protect` wrappers with ZERO production callers. `render_move_phase` has exactly 2 edges into the subgraph, both inside its Sleep Talk block -- the `sleeptalk_refusal_is_unsafe_with_protect` predicate at `rust/pokezero-search/src/events.rs:2138` and the slug emit at `:2159`. Only the second produces a KEY; the first is a boolean test whose result is discarded. So the tail is always a SLEEP TALK CALLEE'S tail, and the bucket needs `sleeptalk` and a drain move ON THE SAME SET. Measured per set, the instrument section 8 requires for a two-thing gap: 44 of 393 sets carry `sleeptalk`, 3 carry a drain move, and 0 carry both. The bucket is therefore UNEMITTABLE in this format, which is strictly stronger than the row's "unambiguous". Shell Bell, the other half of the name, is implemented AS drain (`src/gen3/items.rs`, arm `Items::SHELLBELL`, sets `attacking_choice.drain`), so it produces a byte-identical `Heal` -- the ambiguity is real by construction and not by enumeration -- and it is absent from the 13-item universe.

R14.candidate: N5 -- the residual ceiling overshooting into a move-KO
R14.correction: ⚠ **The corrected argument still had a hole, in the same cross-side family the row already carries a ⚠ for.** It rests entirely on Wonder Guard and never asks whether the OPPONENT can take Wonder Guard away. In gen3 the two moves that can are Skill Swap ([] of 220) and Role Play ([]); Gastro Acid, Worry Seed, Entrainment, Simple Beam and Mold Breaker are all gen4+. Both are 0, so the route is closed -- but nothing had closed it until it was measured. Transform is in the pool (['ditto', 'mew'] species) and is not a route either: it copies the target's ability onto the user and does not copy HP. ⚠ **And the exhaustive type enumeration the row is proud of is VACUOUS.** "Of the pool's 125 moves, every move that is super-effective against Bug/Ghost is single-hit" is true, but so is 'every move in the pool except Bonemerang is single-hit' -- the multi-hit census already gave the whole result and the type scan adds nothing. It is kept here (17 moves, all single-hit) as a control, not as the argument. ⚠ The argument the row does not make is stronger and simpler, and c129 made it: `residual_disjoint_bands` admits a band only under `0 < threshold < ceiling`, and at the TWO KILL sites -- which are the two the N5 ceiling sits in -- that `ceiling` is `defender_active.hp`. So at `hit_count == 1` the arm deals strictly less than the defender's HP by construction and cannot overshoot into a KO, and Shedinja's `hp == 1` makes `0 < threshold < 1` unsatisfiable, so no band is ever built for the one species that motivated the row. ⚠ Scoped to the kill sites deliberately: a first revision wrote `ceiling = defender.hp` flat, and it is `i16::MAX` at the other TWO of the four call sites (the survive mirrors). The argument holds where it is used; the sentence did not hold as written. ⚠ Finally, the row says "the N5 code" as though there were one site: the same `(threshold + hit_count - 1) / hit_count` ceiling appears TWICE in `src/gen3/generate_instructions.rs`, at `residual_per_hit` and at `crit_residual_per_hit` on the crit-straddle branch, so a reader checking one of them has checked half.
R14.demonstration: N5 needs `maxhp <= 47` AND `hit_count > 1`. Over 24,000 generated Pokemon the minimum max HP is 1 and the only species at or below 47 is ['Shedinja']. The pool's only multi-hit move is Bonemerang (Ground); `getEffectiveness('Ground', ['Bug','Ghost'])` is -1 -- resisted, not immune -- so Wonder Guard blocks it. Enumerated exhaustively over the pool's 125 moves: 17 are super-effective against Bug/Ghost and EVERY ONE is single-hit.

R21.candidate: Reflect / Light Screen keeping a trailing float position in the damage pipeline
R21.correction: ⚠ **The row flags itself for re-checking and then answers with an assertion.** "`engine_world` *can construct* screens as side conditions -- but no battle path reaches that state" is the shape this pass exists to replace, and re-tracing it moves where the closure sits. It is NOT `side_condition_unsupported` (`src/pokezero/engine_world.py:1360`): that fires for a condition OUTSIDE the map, and `reflect`, `lightscreen`, `safeguard` and `mist` are all INSIDE it, with turn counters derived rather than copied. If a screen ever appeared, engine_world would build it. The only thing that keeps it from appearing is the protocol: a mapped condition enters solely through a `|-sidestart|` line, and no pool Pokemon can emit one for a screen -- with no copier route either, since `metronome`, `assist`, `mirrormove`, `mimic`, `sketch`, `naturepower` and `magiccoat` are each 0 and Sleep Talk draws from the user's own slots. `spikes` (['cacturne', 'cloyster', 'deoxysdefense', 'deoxysspeed', 'forretress', 'glalie', 'omastar', 'qwilfish', 'roselia', 'skarmory', 'smeargle'] species) is the live control on the same map. ⚠ One capability the row does not mention and that is not a battle path: the scenario harness injects arbitrary side conditions at `src/pokezero/local_showdown.py:2005`. No committed scenario under `scenarios/` sets one, so it is the same shape as the row's own parenthetical -- recorded rather than left to be found again.
R21.demonstration: `reflect`, `lightscreen`, `safeguard`, `mist` are each **0 of 220** species. No Pokemon in the pool can set a screen, and the construction capability the row flags is traced rather than waved at: `_build_side_spec` maps side conditions through `_SIDE_CONDITION_IDS` (`src/pokezero/engine_world.py:118`), which DOES carry `reflect`, `lightscreen`, `safeguard` and `mist`, and refuses an unmapped one at `:1360`. The values it maps come from `side_payload['sideConditions']`, filled from `replay.side_condition_counts` at `src/pokezero/local_showdown.py:2321`, whose live writer is the `-sidestart` arm of the protocol fold. A screen therefore needs a `|-sidestart|…|move: Reflect` line, which needs a pool Pokemon to use the move. `spikes` is the control: it is the one mapped condition the pool CAN set (['cacturne', 'cloyster', 'deoxysdefense', 'deoxysspeed', 'forretress', 'glalie', 'omastar', 'qwilfish', 'roselia', 'skarmory', 'smeargle'] species), so the map is not dead.

Half that list is live in ordinary play. **Nothing opens**, and that is a SET EQUALITY, measured on both sides: the arm's alternatives parsed out of the committed patch are ['ENCORE', 'MIMIC', 'MIRRORMOVE', 'SKETCH', 'STRUGGLE', 'TRANSFORM'], and the non-`Future` gen3 moves carrying Showdown's `failencore` flag -- the condition `encore.condition.onStart` actually tests -- are ['ENCORE', 'MIMIC', 'MIRRORMOVE', 'SKETCH', 'STRUGGLE', 'TRANSFORM']. Equal, so the shipped list is right for its three reachable members too. ⚠ A first revision called this machine-checked while the pin asserted six MEMBERSHIPS, which review defeated by adding `Choices::TACKLE` to the arm and watching the module stay green. The clause is withdrawn; the patch is not. (2) "closes `_HIDDEN_INFORMATION_REQUEST_FLAGS`'s `maybeDisabled`/`maybeLocked`" uses the wrong verb. That frozenset (`src/pokezero/engine_world.py:219`) is a TOLERATE-list: its members are filtered OUT of the refusal binding at `:456`, so those two flags never caused a refusal to begin with. R22.demonstration: `mimic`, `imprison`, `psychup`, `metronome`, `assist`, `naturepower`, `sketch`, `mirrormove` are each **0 of 220** species. Whole-pool absence, side-independent -- which matters for `imprison`, whose producer runs on the FOE (`onFoeDisableMove`), because both teams draw from the same 220-species pool. `maybeDisabled` has exactly one `= true` site in the whole Showdown tree, inside `imprison.condition.onFoeDisableMove`, and gen3 does not override that condition; `maybeLocked` has no `= true` site outside the gen1 partial-trapping mod and in gen3 is definitionally `maybeLocked || maybeDisabled`. G32 closes with `psychup` at 0, because the only in-pool move-caller is Sleep Talk (44 sets) and it selects from the user's OWN move slots.

R4.correction: ⚠ **The row's sentence "The expiry path has no trigger" is FALSE.** The order-8 decrement-and-clear block fires on every Rain Dance (['gorebyss', 'huntail', 'kingdra', 'ludicolo', 'mantine', 'omastar', 'seaking'] species) and Sunny Day (['exeggutor', 'sunflora', 'tangela', 'victreebel']), and `weather_survives_upkeep` evaluates FALSE on their expiring turn -- the expiry path is exercised in ordinary play. What has no trigger is the narrower thing the row is titled after: a chipping weather with a FINITE counter. Rain and sun do not chip; sand and hail are the only chipping weathers and neither can hold a finite counter in this pool. The verdict survives; the sentence that carried it does not. Two neighbouring over-readings are corrected with it: permanent (`-1`) weather is NOT Tyranitar-only -- Kyogre's Drizzle and Groudon's Drought write it too -- and the payload-seeding lane cannot inject finite sand either, but by a different mechanism the row does not cite. ⚠ Stated precisely, because a first revision of this correction wrote "`_weather_fields` returns `-1` ONLY under `weatherFromAbility`" and that is false -- it also returns `("none", -1)` at `src/pokezero/engine_world.py:941` for absent or `none` weather, which is the commonest case in the corpus. The accurate statement is narrower: `-1` for a NAMED weather requires `weatherFromAbility`, and a prefix that saw only `[upkeep]` lines fails closed at `weather_turns_unknown` rather than fabricating a counter, so the seeding lane cannot inject finite sand.
R4.demonstration: `sandstorm`, `hail` are each **0 of 220** species as moves, so the only sand writer left is Sand Stream -- carried by ['tyranitar'] alone, on all 3 of its 3 sets -- which writes `WEATHER_ABILITY_TURNS = -1` (`src/gen3/abilities.rs`, symbol `ability_on_switch_in`, arm `Abilities::SANDSTREAM`). The expiry block in `add_end_of_turn_instructions` is guarded on `state.weather.turns_remaining > 0`, which `-1` fails, so permanent sand is never decremented and never reaches the `== 0` clear. The chip gate is a SEPARATE expression, `weather_survives_upkeep = turns_remaining != 1`, and `weather_chips` returns `Some` only for HAIL or SAND -- so `turns_remaining == 1` and a chipping weather cannot coincide.

Closed here by measurement: `trick` is ['furret', 'kecleon'] of 220 species and `knockoff` ['banette', 'hariyama', 'lickitung', 'sableye'], and both only SWAP or REMOVE; `thief`, `covet`, `recycle`, `switcheroo` and `bugbite` are each 0, and no gen3 mechanism CREATES an item.
